About Geo Server Data Downloader

Geo Server Data Downloader is a project I built to make working with GIS data simpler and more accessible. As someone who works with geospatial data, I know how frustrating it can be to find a dataset, download it from a web service, and get it into the format you actually need.

Why I Built It

Sometimes, a task as simple as downloading data from an ArcGIS REST service or converting GeoJSON to KML requires desktop software, command-line tools, or a separate online service. I wanted to make these everyday tasks easier, so I started building a tool that brings them together in one place. My goal was to create a practical GIS tool that people could use without installing additional software or creating an account.

I wanted to build a unified platform that:

  • Work directly in your browser, without uploading your files to a server I control.
  • Download spatial data from ArcGIS REST services and explore publicly available layers on ArcGIS Online.
  • Convert common GIS formats, including Shapefile, GeoJSON, KML, GeoPackage, CSV, and GPX.
  • Preview layers on an interactive map and inspect their attribute tables before exporting.
  • Make everyday GIS data tasks available for free, without artificial feature limits or paywalls.

That's exactly what Geo Server Data Downloader delivers. It's the comprehensive tool I wished existed when I first started working with GIS data.

Credits and Open Source

Geo Server Data Downloader is based in part on geodatadownloader, an open-source project by Myles Haynes released under the MIT License. The core download approach (reading a layer's object IDs, fetching features in small pages, and converting the result in the browser) and the WFS support follow that project's design, with modifications.

What this site adds: the ArcGIS Online discovery tool, the browser-based GIS file converter, the documentation, and the guides in the blog. The full license text is in the third-party notices.

What You Can Do With the Tool

Geo Server Data Downloader provides three main workflows:

  • Load data directly from a URL : Paste any ArcGIS REST Paste an ArcGIS REST FeatureServer, MapServer, or supported WFS endpoint to inspect the service, browse its available layers, and preview spatial data on an interactive map. You can then view the attribute table and export the data in a supported format.
  • Discover public ArcGIS Online layers : Search for publicly available feature services and open data layers on ArcGIS Online. This is useful when you know what data you're looking for but don't already have a service URL.
  • Convert your existing GIS files : Upload supported spatial files from your computer and convert them into another format directly in your browser. You can use this workflow to prepare data for different GIS applications without needing a separate conversion program.

The original files remain on your computer during local file conversion, and the tool is designed to preserve spatial and attribute information wherever the target format supports it.

Supported GIS Formats

The tool supports the following formats for its applicable download and conversion workflows:

  • Shapefile (.zip) A widely used vector format, packaged with its required supporting files.
  • GeoJSON (.geojson) A convenient format for web mapping and exchanging spatial data.
  • KML (.kml) Useful for Google Earth and other compatible mapping applications.
  • GeoPackage (.gpkg) A versatile, SQLite-based format for storing geospatial data.
  • CSV (.csv) Tabular data, with optional spatial information such as coordinates or WKT geometry.
  • GPX (.gpx) Commonly used for GPS tracks, routes, and waypoints.

Built With Privacy in Mind

Built With Privacy in Mind One of the decisions I made early in development was to keep data processing on the client side. Local file conversion, processing, and export run in your browser using JavaScript and WebAssembly. Files you upload for local processing are not sent to a server I control. When you load data from an external GIS service, your browser communicates directly with that service to retrieve the requested information. This approach helps keep your files under your control while making the tool accessible through an ordinary web browser.

How It Works

Geo Server Data Downloader is built with React, Vite, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and the ArcGIS Maps SDK for JavaScript. For data processing and format conversion, it uses gdal3.js (a WebAssembly port of the industry-standard GDAL library). The application is hosted as a static website, allowing users to access its tools without installing a desktop application.
